To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a combination of thermostabilized enzymes, including scaffoldin, in the form of designer cellulosomes is more effective in degrading cellulosic substratum than the wild-type counterpart.

a thermostable designer cellulosome, composed of thermostable scaffoldins and thermostable cellulosomal components, is more efficient than a conventional designer cellulosome composed of mesophilic enzymes in the conversion of cellulose into soluble sugars.
the combination of thermophilic designer enzymes and a thermoderant scaffoldin resulted in a 1.5-fold increase in cellulosic substrate conversion compared with conventional designer cellulosome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a thermostabilized cellulosome that can function efficiently at high temperatures and is able to degrade cellulose.
the development of designer cellulosomes with enhanced thermostability for the deconstruction of lignocellulosics at elevated temperatures.
the design of thermophilic designer cellulso mes for use in the conversion of biomass into biofuels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of thermostable scaffoldins is a critical parameter for the stability and activity of the designer cellulosomes at elevated temperatures.

the use of thermostable scaffoldins and thermostable cellulolytic enzymes in designer cellulosomes is essential for the development of a stable and effective enzyme system for the deconstruction of cell wall biomass at high temperatures.
The use of thermostable enzyme components in designer cellulosomes is a promising strategy for improving cellulosome-mediated cellulose degradation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
by improving the thermostability of the enzyme sub-units and the structural component of cellulosomes, we have improved cellulosome-mediated degradation of cellulosic materials.
the use of thermophilic enzymes and thermostable scaffoldins for the construction of designer cellulosomes is a promising strategy for the efficient conversion of biomass to soluble sugars.
we have converted conventional designer cellulosome to a thermophilic designer cellulose by using thermostable enzymes and scaffoldin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
simple improvement in the activity and stability of a given enzyme may not guarantee its suitability as a component in multienzymatic systems.
the use of a thermostabilized enzyme cocktail, which contains thermostable scaffoldins, can be used to improve the deconstruction of crystallin cellulose by cellulosome technology.
the use of thermophilic enzymes in designer cellulosomes can be a viable strategy to increase the efficiency of cellulose conversion.
